conviction_note: Two small positives: an expected US tariff refund that the published bar appears to leave out, and a large disclosed short (4.53%, not the baseline's 0.0) facing the founding family's usual report-day buying. H&M's own reaction function cuts both down. Beats have been sold on 3 of the last 3 prints (-0.7, -2.2, -0.6), Pandora fell 1.7% when it booked the same refund, and the family bought on all three of those down days. So the move is held at +0.6 against a findings sum of +0.9. It rests on 26-analyst coverage and on nothing about the September sales line, which is the thing that actually moves this stock.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: a 4.53% disclosed aggregate short, building +0.11pp in the last sessions (the baseline reads it as 0.0 through a name-join failure), sits against the Persson family's Ramsbury bid. The family has bought in size ON the report day of each of the last three prints: 2.0m shares on 2026-01-29, 4.5m on 2026-03-26 and 2.75m on 2026-06-25, each more than a normal day's volume. It was out of the market through the MAR closed period, during which the stock fell from 184.5 (2026-08-24) to 162.5 (2026-09-18).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The family bought on report day in all three 2026 prints and the stock still closed down each time: -0.7% (Q4, 2026-01-29), -2.2% (Q1, 2026-03-26), -0.6% (Q2, 2026-06-25), per Modular's report-day table. The one squeeze in the recent record is Q3 2025, +9.8% on 2025-09-25, on a gross-margin beat. So the bid has cushioned downside and has not produced upside on its own.

findings.why_not_priced: The sealed lean (+0.37) contains only the run-up: its short_squeeze component is 0.0 because the register join missed a 4.53% short. A fully priced squeeze would show up as a stock rallying into the print while the short covered. Instead the short is adding (+0.11pp since the 09-02 level) and the stock drifted 12% lower through the closed period with its largest buyer barred from the tape. The family pattern is public in the FI insider register and in Swedish press, so this is flow timing rather than hidden information, and it is sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: The short level and the family buying come from two different FI registers: https://www.fi.se/sv/vara-register/blankningsregistret/GetBlankningsregisterAggregat/ and the insynsregister above. That the stock drifted without the bid is read off the Yahoo tape (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HM-B.ST?range=3mo&interval=1d). No third source says the setup will squeeze.

findings.finding: A US IEEPA tariff refund of up to SEK 1.5bn (Citi) is likely to land in the Jun-Aug quarter's P&L and appears to be outside the published bar. H&M has said nothing about it on either 2026 call. CBP had paid out about $100bn by 31 July, and Pandora booked a partial refund in its Apr-Jun quarter as a 230bp one-off gross-margin item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H&M has no prior refund print. The closest analogue is Nordic peer Pandora: it booked the refund as a flagged one-off, raised margin guidance explicitly on it, and the stock fell 1.74% on underlying weakness (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/pandora-raises-2026-guidance-on-tariff-refund-q2-growth-93CH-4855608, 2026-08-12). H&M's own last gross-margin beat (Q3 2025) was paid +9.8%, but that was operating margin, not a one-off.
findings.original_quote: Citi uppskattar att H&M kan ha rätt till upp till 1,5 miljarder kronor, även om alla belopp kanske inte hinner begäras eller betalas ut under tredje kvartalet. [Citi estimates H&M may be entitled to up to SEK 1.5bn, although not all of it may be claimed or paid out in the third quarter.]  Also EFN/Direkt 2026-09-22: 'Det finns en liten risk att den rapporterade siffran kommer att se superstark ut, och att man först i efterhand kommer få fram att "Ah, men det ligger ju en miljard i återbetalningar här".' [There is a small risk the reported figure will look super strong and only afterwards will people find 'ah, but there is a billion in refunds in here'.]
findings.why_not_priced: The bar looks like it excludes the refund. Consensus EBIT of SEK 5,095m is only +3.7% y/y, and consensus gross margin of 53.37% matches Citi's own ex-refund 53.3%. If the refund were in the bar, EBIT would be near SEK 6.1-6.6bn. The market already knows about it, though: Citi's note moved the stock +4.05% on 2026-08-18 and the gain has since been fully given back. On close-to-close the market will likely strip a flagged one-off, which is why this is sized at a fraction of the money (SEK 1bn is roughly 3-4% of annual EBIT) and not as a headline 20% EBIT beat. The lessons file's four US refund names split up or down by double digits on guidance direction, so the sign here really belongs to the September sales line, which nobody can see.
findings.independence: Two different Swedish outlets carry the same Citi figure: https://efn.se/handms-akilleshal-i-fokus-infor-rapporten (2026-09-22) and https://www.privataaffarer.se/placeringar/aktier/citi-kladjatten-en-stor-vinnare-vid-tullaterbetalning/ (2026-03-06, 12% of FY EBIT). The Pandora precedent, a different company in a different source, shows that refunds are being booked in these quarters.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the lean (+0.37, run-up only) and with the free control (20d run-up -7.37% implies mean-reversion up). The baseline's positioning read of 0.0 is wrong: the real short is 4.53% and building, which if anything strengthens a positive lean. So there is no tension to haircut. The haircut from +0.9 to +0.6 comes from H&M's reaction function, which has sold beats on 3 of the last 3 prints.
language_note: The Swedish-language FI insider register (insynsregistret) shows the founding family buying 2.0m / 4.5m / 2.75m B shares on the report day itself in January, March and June 2026. No English source searched carried that report-day pattern.

Finansinspektionen's Swedish aggregate register gives the true 4.53% short (position date 2026-09-22), which the baseline's name join missed. The register is a Swedish-language file, and no English preview mentioned the short.

The Swedish previews (Börsvärlden/Modular with 27 estimates, EFN/Direkt with Infront's 15) carried consensus gross margin, EBIT and local-currency growth, the Citi SEK 1.5bn refund estimate, and an analyst warning that the refund may be 'buried in the numbers'. The English previews found (finanzen.ch, defenseworld) carried only EPS and revenue.

The primary filings themselves added nothing language-specific. H&M publishes every report in Swedish and English at once, and the English call transcript was the only readable source for the Q3 gross-margin guide.
lessons_applied: 'Name the line' / the US tariff-refund names split by double digits on guidance: I cut the refund one_off from +0.4 to +0.3 and widened its low end from -1.0 to -1.5, because on this line the sign follows the guide (the September sales statement), not the refund.

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' / hunter's caveat must reach the number: I cut expected_move from +0.7 to +0.6 against a +0.9 sum, because H&M's reported beats were sold on 3 of 3 prints in 2026, family buying included.

'A zero on a register that read is the truncation floor' pushed me to check the register directly. It turned out the zero was neither a floor nor a measurement but a join failure (4.53% actual). That check was already done before reading the file, so the positioning finding stays at +0.6.
